servidor-openai-compativel.d: An HTTP server that implements the routes and JSON fields of the OpenAI API (/v1/models, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/responses). Changing the base_url is enough for the same SDK or agent to talk to a different model. vllm serve brings one up.

extra-body.d: An option of the OpenAI Python SDK that merges extra fields (e.g., chat_template_kwargs, vllm_xargs) into the top level of the JSON. It is not a protocol field: in raw HTTP, send those fields directly at the top level.

vllm-xargs.d: A free-form dictionary of extra per-request arguments that vLLM forwards to the sampling parameters. Overlays use it to add options without breaking clients, such as GLM's skip_writing_prefix_cache.

sse.d: An HTTP streaming format in which the server sends data: {json} lines separated by a blank line, ending with data: [DONE]. Each event carries only the new delta. It is append-only: what has been sent cannot be undone.

finish-reason.d: The reason a choice stopped: stop (EOS or a stop string), length (ran out of max_tokens or of context), tool_calls (ended with a complete call) or abort. Clients should discard incomplete calls when length comes back.

chat-template-kwargs.d: A dictionary sent by the client whose keys become variables inside the template: it turns reasoning on/off (enable_thinking/thinking) and picks the effort (reasoning_effort). Valid names and values change from family to family. --default-chat-template-kwargs sets the server default.

reasoning-parser.d: An API server component (--reasoning-parser) that puts the text between <think> and </think> into the reasoning field and the rest into content. It marks the boundary at which stops, the grammar and tool-call extraction take effect.

detokenizer-incremental.d: The part of vLLM that converts IDs into text at every step, keeping offsets so it only emits complete UTF-8 characters. It is where EOS and stop strings are checked, in a window that covers stops split across tokens.

stop-string.d: Text (e.g., "Question:") that ends generation when it appears in the output. It can span tokens, so the search looks at the new characters plus the |s|−1 before them. In reasoning models, the GLM and DeepSeek recipes keep it dormant until </think>.

tool-calling.d: A protocol in which the model writes, in its own format, a structured request to run a function. The server converts it into JSON tool_calls, and the client runs the function and sends the result back in a role: "tool" message. The model itself executes nothing.

tool-call-parser.d: The translator (--tool-call-parser: glm47, qwen3_coder, deepseek_v4) from each family's call markup into OpenAI tool_calls. When streaming, it works as a state machine (text → opening → name → arguments → closing).

tool-choice.d: The request field that controls calls: auto (the model decides; requires --enable-auto-tool-choice), none (the client wants no call; in stock vLLM it only suppresses the returned tool_calls, without constraining generation), required (at least one) or named (exactly that function). It goes hand in hand with parallel_tool_calls and strict.

logit-masking.d: Zeroing out the probability of forbidden tokens before sampling by setting their logits to −∞ (mask m ∈ {0,1}). It is the mechanism behind bad_words, required/named tool_choice and structured outputs, and it holds at any temperature.

bad-words.d: A list of forbidden strings in a vLLM request. A single-token word is masked at every position, including the draft positions of speculative verification. A multi-token word only has its last token blocked once the previous ones have come out.

dsml.d: DeepSeek-V4's tool-call markup: <｜DSML｜tool_calls>, <｜DSML｜invoke name=…>, <｜DSML｜parameter …>. A single malformed structural token keeps the deepseek_v4 parser from recognizing the call.

contrato-fail-closed.d: A layer that checks, after generation, whether the response meets the requested contract (in DeepSeek's hotfix #191: cardinality, name and arguments valid against the strict schema for named or required tool_choice). Violations are regenerated and, once the attempts run out, become HTTP 500 instead of a silently wrong 200.

structured-outputs.d: Generation constrained by a grammar (JSON schema, regex, choice, EBNF, structural tag). At every step, only the tokens that keep the output valid can be sampled. In vLLM it is requested through response_format or structured_outputs.

xgrammar.d: vLLM's default structured-outputs backend. It compiles the grammar into a pushdown automaton, precomputes per state the tokens that can be decided without context and, at every step, fills in a bitmask of allowed tokens (accept_tokens, validate_tokens, rollback).

token-bitmask.d: A vector with 1 bit per vocabulary token (1 = allowed), packed into 32-bit integers: 4·⌈V/32⌉ bytes per row (19,360 B on GLM). There is one row per sequence and, with speculation, one per draft position.

structural-tag.d: A kind of constraint in which the grammar only activates inside a region opened by a trigger (e.g., the DSML tool-call block), leaving the rest of the text free. It is used to enforce named or required tool_choice.

responses-api.d: The OpenAI-family /v1/responses API, with typed items (message, function_call, reasoning…) and named SSE events. It allows stateless replay (store:false) or stateful continuation (store:true + previous_response_id), whose state lives in the server's memory.

bearer-token.d: An HTTP scheme in which the client sends Authorization: Bearer <key>. In vLLM it is turned on by --api-key/VLLM_API_KEY. The flag is a list (nargs): several keys go in a single occurrence, because repeating the flag overwrites it.

guarded-prefix.d: The set of route prefixes that vLLM's Bearer middleware protects: /v1, /v2, /inference (and /cohere, according to GLM). Root routes such as /tokenize, /metrics, /invocations and the cache resets answer without a key.

call-inteira.d: Streaming policy in which the server follows a tool call while it is being written but only sends it once it closes, in a single delta with header and arguments. A call the reply ends inside is never sent. It is patch 0053's rule in the GLM TensorFold lane, the opposite of vLLM's argument-fragment streaming.

keepalive-sse.d: An event sent only to show the connection is alive when there is no new content. In the GLM TensorFold lane, an empty delta goes out every 2 s while a tool call is held, for clients that drop idle connections.

raciocinio-intercalado.d: Template pattern in which the reasoning of each assistant step in a tool loop is rendered back into the prompt. On GLM-5.3 it applies to the steps after the last user message. If the client does not send that reasoning back, the template puts <think></think> in its place.

context-length-exceeded.d: OpenAI API error code for a request whose prompt plus output limit does not fit the model's window. Agent clients use it as the signal to compact the conversation. In the GLM TensorFold lane it comes as HTTP 400, with param naming the field (messages or prompt).

marcacao-por-id.d: Splitting reasoning, answer and tool calls by the ids of the marker tokens the model generated (</think>, <tool_call>…), not by the decoded text: a marker merely quoted as text stays text. In the GLM·TF recipe, patches 0116 (input) and 0117 (output).
